1 Purpose

This file is part of a research compendium (Pierce, 2026). It provides some descriptive analyses of data provided by Alison Masyr and Caitlin Eliason that contains observations of dogs receiving CHOP chemotherapy at MSU Veterinary Medicine Clinic (VMC) between 2016 and 2022. Some results here are used in a manuscript (Eliason et al., 2026).

2 Setup

This section of the report documents some setup tasks that are useful to the statistician on the team. Most readers of this report will probably want skip directly to Section 3.

2.1 Define Global Options

Global R chunk options are defined in the YAML header but local chunk options will over-ride global options. We can temporarily disable an individual chunk by inserting #| eval: false on a line at the top of the chunk.

3 Results

3.1 Patient-Level Summaries

Table 2 and Table 3 show summaries of missing data in the patient-level dataset.

Code 
```{r}
#| label: tbl-patient-cvv-missing
#| tbl-cap: "Missingness Overview for Patient-Level Dataset (`Final_Patients`): 
#|          Cases, Variables, and Values"

Final_Patients %>% 
  cvv_missingness() %>% 
  kable(format = "html", digits = 1,
          col.names = c("Subset", rep(c("n", "%"), times = 3))) %>%
    kable_styling() %>%
    add_header_above(header = c(" " = 1, "Cases" = 2, "Variables" = 2, "Values" = 2))
```
Code 
```{r}
#| label: tbl-patient-var-missing
#| tbl-cap: Misssingness Assessment for Variables in Patient-Level Dataset 
#|          (`Final_Patients`)

Final_Patients %>% 
var_missingness(.) %>% 
  kable(format = "html", digits = 1) %>%
  kable_styling() %>%
  add_header_above(header = c(" " = 3, "Observed Values" = 2, 
                              "Missing Values" = 2))
```

Table 4 shows patient-level descriptive statistics for weight surface area, and number of visits, while Table 12 gives the univariate frequency distribution for leukemic status, which was a time-invariant patient-level characteristic within the CHOP cycle.

Code 
```{r}
#| label: tbl-patient-describe
#| tbl-cap: !expr paste0("Descriptive Statistics for Patient-Level Variables ", 
#|                       "(N = ", nrow(Final_Patients), " Patients)")
#| message: false

VNames <- c("Age_Yrs", "Weight_kg", "Surface_Area_m2", "N_Visits")

CNames <- c("Variable", "N", "Mean", "SD", "Min", "Q25", "Q50", "Q75", "Max")

Final_Patients %>% 
  select(Age_Yrs, Weight_kg, Surface_Area_m2, N_Visits) %>% 
  pivot_longer(cols = c(Age_Yrs, Weight_kg, Surface_Area_m2, N_Visits), 
               names_to = "Variable", values_to = "Value") %>% 
  mutate(Variable = factor(Variable, levels = VNames)) %>% 
  # Aggregate to one row per variable.
  group_by(Variable) %>% 
  summarise(N = sum(!is.na(Value)), 
            Mean = mean(Value, na.rm = TRUE),
            SD = sd(Value, na.rm = TRUE),
            Min = min(Value, na.rm = TRUE),
            Q25 = quantile(Value, probs = .25, na.rm = TRUE),
            Q50 = quantile(Value, probs = .50, na.rm = TRUE),
            Q75 = quantile(Value, probs = .75, na.rm = TRUE),
            Max = max(Value, na.rm = TRUE)) %>% 
  kable(., format = "html", digits = 2, 
        col.names = CNames, row.names = FALSE) %>% 
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"),
                fixed_thead = T)
```
Code 
```{r}
#| label: weight

N_Weight_LT10 <- Final_Patients %>% filter(Weight_kg < 10) %>% nrow()
N_Weight_1015 <- Final_Patients %>% filter(between(Weight_kg, left = 10, right = 15)) %>% nrow()

Pct_Weight_LT10 <- 100*N_Weight_LT10/nrow(Final_Patients)
Pct_Weight_1015 <- 100*N_Weight_1015/nrow(Final_Patients)
```

Caution

Using Stage as a predictor in the model would be complicated by the fact that there is only one patient with Stage = 1 and none with Stage = 2. Meanwhile, some patients have missing Stage data because they have diseases to which staging does not apply, while others just have true missing data. Given the size and heterogeneity of the sample, I think omitting Stage as a model predictor of bandemia seems like the wiser choice.

Caution

Code 
```{r}
#| label: tbl-visit-var-missing
#| tbl-cap: Misssingness Assessment for Variables in Visit-Level Dataset

var_missingness(.) %>%
```

Table 15 shows univariate frequency distributions for binary categorical biomarker variables. The Is_Sick variable is a binary transform of Sick_Type; it has a lot of missing values because we only collected Sick_Type for observations with Total_Bands > 0 (equivalent to Bands_Present = 1 (i.e., Yes)).

Code 
```{r}
#| label: tbl-visit-describe-cat
#| tbl-cap: !expr paste0("Descriptive Statistics for Categorical Biomarker ", 
#|                       "Variables (N = ", nrow(Final_Visits), " Visits)")
#| message: false

VNames <- c("Bands_Present", "Bandemia", "High_BN_Ratio", "Is_Sick", 
            "Toxic_Change")

Final_Visits %>% 
  select(Bands_Present, Bandemia, High_BN_Ratio, Is_Sick, Toxic_Change) %>% 
  pivot_longer(cols = c(Bands_Present, Bandemia, High_BN_Ratio, Is_Sick, 
                        Toxic_Change), 
               names_to = "Variable", values_to = "Value") %>% 
  group_by(Variable, Value, .drop = FALSE) %>% 
  summarise(N = n()) %>% 
  mutate(Variable = factor(Variable, levels = VNames),
         Value = factor(Value, levels=0:1, labels = c("No", "Yes")),
         Percent = 100*(N/nrow(Final_Visits))) %>% 
  arrange(Variable, desc(Value)) %>% 
  mutate(Variable = factor(Variable, levels = VNames)) %>% 
  kable(., format = "html", digits = 1, row.names = FALSE) %>% 
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"),
                fixed_thead = T) %>% 
  collapse_rows(., columns = 1, valign = "top", 
                row_group_label_position = "stack") 
```

Table 16 shows the frequency distribution of the 4-level Sick_Type variable across all observations. This variable has a lot of missing values because we only collected Sick_Type for observations with Total_Bands > 0 (equivalent to Bands_Present = 1 (i.e., Yes)). Self-limited means that sickness was not treated with either medication or hospitalization.

Code 
```{r}
#| label: tbl-visit-Sick-Type
#| tbl-cap: !expr paste0("Frequency Distribution for Sick Type ", 
#|                       "(N = ", nrow(Final_Visits), " Visits)")
#| message: false

Final_Visits %>% 
  count(Sick_Type) %>% 
  rename(N_Visits = n) %>% 
  mutate(Percent = 100*(N_Visits/nrow(Final_Visits))) %>% 
  kbl(digits = 1) %>%
  kable_styling()
```

Table 17 shows the frequency distribution for 3-level ordinal band category variable.

Code 
```{r}
#| label: tbl-visit-band-category
#| tbl-cap: !expr paste0("Frequency Distribution for Band Category ", 
#|                       "(N = ", nrow(Final_Visits), " Visits)")
#| message: false

Final_Visits %>%

  rename(N_Visits = n) %>% 
  mutate(Percent = 100*(N_Visits/nrow(Final_Visits))) %>%

  kable_styling()
```

Table 18 shows the crosstabulation of whether bands were present and whether toxic change was observed in the CBC sample in the visit-level data. This was initially used to investigate missing data issues that we have subsequently fixed.

Code 
```{r}
#| label: tbl-visit-bands-toxic
#| tbl-cap: !expr paste0("Crosstab of Bands Present by Toxic Change ", 
#|                       "(N = ", nrow(Final_Visits), " Visits)")

Final_Visits %>% 
  mutate(Bands_Present = factor(Bands_Present, levels = 0:1, 
                                labels = c("No", "Yes")),
         Toxic_Change = factor(Toxic_Change, levels = 0:1, 
                                labels = c("No", "Yes"))) %>% 
  xtabs(~Toxic_Change + Bands_Present , addNA = TRUE, data = .) %>% 
  addmargins() %>% 
  as.data.frame() %>% 
  pivot_wider(names_from = Bands_Present, values_from = Freq) %>% 
  kable(., format = "html", digits = 1, row.names = FALSE) %>% 
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"),
                fixed_thead = T) %>% 
  row_spec(row = 3, italic = TRUE) %>% 
  column_spec(column = 4, italic = TRUE) %>% 
  add_header_above(header = c(" ", "Bands_Present" = 2, " "))
```
Tip

Table 18 shows that all of the instances of toxic change are for CBC samples where bands were present. Per Dr. Masyr, toxic change is a description given to mature neutrophils, not bands (though both can be simultaneously present).

Table 19 shows visit-level descriptive statistics for continuous biomarker variables, while Table 20 repeats the same summary broken down by whether banedmia was absent versus present at the time of the CBC sample.

Code 
```{r}
#| label: tbl-visit-describe-cont
#| tbl-cap: !expr paste0("Descriptive Statistics for Continuous Biomarker ", 
#|                       "Variables (N = ", nrow(Final_Visits), " Visits)")
#| message: false

VNames <- c("Total_WBC", "Total_Neutrophil", "Total_Bands", "BN_Ratio")
VNamesUnits <- c("Total_WBC (k/ul)", 
                 "Total_Neutrophil (k/ul)", 
                 "Total_Bands (k/ul)", 
                 "BN_Ratio")

CNames <- c("Variable", "N", "Mean", "SD", "Min", "Q25", "Q50", "Q75", "Max")

Final_Visits %>% 
  select(Total_WBC, Total_Neutrophil, Total_Bands, BN_Ratio) %>% 
  pivot_longer(cols = c(Total_WBC, Total_Neutrophil, Total_Bands, BN_Ratio), 
               names_to = "Variable", values_to = "Value") %>% 
  mutate(Variable = factor(Variable, levels = VNames)) %>% 
  # Aggregate to one row per variable.
  group_by(Variable) %>% 
  summarise(N = sum(!is.na(Value)), 
            Mean = mean(Value, na.rm = TRUE),
            SD = sd(Value, na.rm = TRUE),
            Min = min(Value, na.rm = TRUE),
            Q25 = quantile(Value, probs = .25, na.rm = TRUE),
            Q50 = quantile(Value, probs = .50, na.rm = TRUE),
            Q75 = quantile(Value, probs = .75, na.rm = TRUE),
            Max = max(Value, na.rm = TRUE)) %>% 
  ungroup() %>% 
  mutate(Variable = factor(Variable, levels = VNames, labels = VNamesUnits)) %>% 
  kable(., format = "html", digits = 1, 
        col.names = CNames, row.names = FALSE) %>% 
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"),
                fixed_thead = T) 
```
Code 
```{r}
#| label: fig-visit-bands-neuts
#| fig-cap: !expr paste0("Scatterplot of Total Bands and Total Neutrophils ", 
#|                       "With Linear and Loess Smoothing Curves ",
#|                       "(N = ", nrow(Final_Visits), " Visits)")
#| fig-width: 4
#| fig-height: 2.64
#| warning: false

Fig1 <- Final_Visits %>% 
  ggplot(., aes(x = Total_Neutrophil, y = Total_Bands)) + 
  geom_point() +
  stat_correlation(method = "pearson", small.r = TRUE, r.conf.level = 0.95, 
                   use_label("R", "R.CI", "n")) +
  geom_smooth(method="loess", se = TRUE, fullrange = FALSE, 
              level = 0.95, linetype = "dashed", col = "red") +
  geom_smooth(method="lm", se = TRUE, fullrange = FALSE, level = 0.95, 
              linetype = "solid", col = "red") +
  theme_bw() +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, 50), ylim = c(0, 7), ) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(from = 0, to = 50, by = 10)) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(from = 0, to = 7, by = 1)) +
  xlab("Total neutrophils (k/ul)") +
  ylab("Total bands (k/ul)") +
  annotate(geom = "text", x =45, y = 4.6, label = "Loess", col = "red") +
  annotate(geom = "text", x =45, y = 2.5, label = "Linear", col = "red") 

Fig1

# Export figure for use in journal submission
ggsave(filename = here(paste0("scripts/output/Figure_1.png")), plot = Fig1, 
       device = "png", width = 4, height = 2.64, units = "in", dpi = 600)
```
Tip

Figure 1 will be Figure 1 in the manuscript we are preparing (Eliason et al., 2026). Note that the Pearson correlation is specifically a measure of linear association.

```{r}

Final_Visits %>% 
  select(Name, Dose_mgpm2) %>% 
  pivot_longer(cols = c(Dose_mgpm2), 
               names_to = "Variable", values_to = "Value") %>% 
  mutate(Variable = factor(VNames, levels = VNames)) %>% 
  # Aggregate to one row per variable.
  group_by(Name) %>% 
  summarise(Variable = VNames,
            N = sum(!is.na(Value)), 
            Mean = mean(Value, na.rm = TRUE),
            SD = sd(Value, na.rm = TRUE),
            Min = min(Value, na.rm = TRUE),
            Q25 = quantile(Value, probs = .25, na.rm = TRUE),
            Q50 = quantile(Value, probs = .50, na.rm = TRUE),
            Q75 = quantile(Value, probs = .75, na.rm = TRUE),
            Max = max(Value, na.rm = TRUE)) %>% 
  ungroup() %>% 
  mutate(Variable = factor(Variable, levels = VNames, labels = VNamesUnits)) %>% 
  kable(., format = "html", digits = 1, 
        col.names = CNames, row.names = FALSE) %>% 
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"),
                fixed_thead = T) 
```
Caution

Dosage is a visit-level (L1) variable. The three drugs have very different ranges of typical values for dosage: The ranges differ by multiple orders of magnitude. Furthermore, there is no good reason expect that the dosage effect would have the same slope for across drugs. To use dosage in the model, we would need to center it, aggregate it to L2 means, then include main effect and interaction terms at both L1 and L2 between dosage and drug. We would also need to consider non-linear dosage effects. The interactions would permit the dosage effect to vary across drugs but this, plus considering non-linearity, would add a lot of parameters to the model. Given the sample size, that seems overly ambitious. It seems better to omit dosage effects from the model. I am not confident our data are sufficient to get reliable findings about dosage effects.

Figure 3 shows the distribution of log-transformed total bands via both a histogram and a boxplot with jittered data points. It includes data from all visits. In both graphs, the log equals -Infinity when total bands are 0, so we recoded these values to improve the figures and keep them compact and readable.

```{r}

  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(-5.1, 2), breaks = c(-5, -3:2),

  scale_y_continuous(limits=c(-0.1, 500)) +

  ylab("No. of Patients") +
  ggtitle("Histogram")

p2 <- Final_Visits %>%

  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(-5, 2)) +

  xlab("log(Total Bands [k/ul])")  +

p1 + p2 +

  plot_annotation(tag_levels = "A")
```

3.4 Bandemia by Visit Number

Table 35 and Figure 22 show that there is not a simple functional form for the relationship between visit number and bandemia rate. It is probably not viable to model a visit effect in this study because of this and because of the structural association of visit number with which drug was used (see Figure 23 in the Drug Sequences section). Also note that the bandemia rate at visit 10 should be interpreted with caution because of the tiny sample size.

Code 
```{r}
#| label: tbl-bandemia-by-visit
#| tbl-cap: Bandemia Rate by Visit Number

Final_Visits %>% 
  group_by(Visit_Number) %>% 
  summarize(N = n(),
            Bandemia = mean(Bandemia)) %>%
  kable(format = "html", digits = 2) %>% 
  kable_styling()
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-bandemia-by-visit

  ggplot(., aes(x = Visit_Number, y = Bandemia)) +

  scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(1:10), minor_breaks = NULL) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0,.36), 
                     breaks = seq(from = 0, to = .35, by = .05),
                     minor_breaks = NULL) +
```


3.8 Drug Sequences

Table 39 shows the frequency of occurrence for each unique sequence of drug use observed. Each row represents a group of dogs who got the same sequence of drugs across the 10 visits of interest. Ideally, the most common sequence will match the intended CHOP protocol sequence for using the drugs. The table is sorted in descending order by sequence frequency (N_Dogs) then by N_Visits, which is the number of visits in the pattern that were actually observed. Columns V1 to V10 show the drug number used at a specific visit number in the given sequence. Because only data about drugs 1-3 were included, it is possible that blanks in the middle of a sequence were visits where some other drug was administered.

Code 
```{r}
#| label: tbl-visit-patterns
#| tbl-cap: !expr paste0("Frequency Distribution of Drug Sequence ", 
#|                       "(N = ", length(unique(Final_Visits$Patient)), 
#|                       " Patients)")
#| warning: false

options(knitr.kable.NA = '-')

Final_Visits %>% 
  select(Patient, Visit_Number, Drug) %>% 
  rename(VN = Visit_Number) %>% 
  pivot_wider(id_cols = "Patient", names_from = "VN", names_prefix = "V", 
              values_from = "Drug") %>% 
  group_by(V1, V2, V3, V4, V5, V6, V7, V8, V9, V10) %>% 
  summarize(N_Dogs = n()) %>% 
  ungroup() %>% 
  rowwise() %>% 
  mutate(N_Visits = sum(!is.na(c_across(V1:V10)))) %>% 
  ungroup() %>% 
  arrange(desc(N_Dogs), desc(N_Visits)) %>% 
  rowid_to_column(var = "SequenceID") %>% 
  relocate(SequenceID, N_Dogs, N_Visits) %>% 
  kable() %>%
  kable_styling() %>% 
  add_header_above(header = c(" " = 3, "Drug Sequence (Drug Used by Visit Number)" = 10))
```

Table 40 shows the subset of drug sequences that deviate from the CHOP protocol by using cyclosphosphamide at visit 1.

Code 
```{r}
#| label: tbl-visit-patterns-subset
#| tbl-cap: !expr paste0("Subset of Drug Sequences That Used Cyclosphosphamide ", 
#|                       "at Visit 1 ",
#|                       "(N = ", length(unique(Final_Visits$Patient)), 
#|                       " Patients)")
#| warning: false

options(knitr.kable.NA = '-')

Final_Visits %>% 
  select(Patient, Visit_Number, Drug) %>% 
  rename(VN = Visit_Number) %>% 
  pivot_wider(id_cols = "Patient", names_from = "VN", names_prefix = "V", 
              values_from = "Drug") %>% 
  group_by(V1, V2, V3, V4, V5, V6, V7, V8, V9, V10) %>% 
  summarize(N_Dogs = n()) %>% 
  ungroup() %>% 
  rowwise() %>% 
  mutate(N_Visits = sum(!is.na(c_across(V1:V10)))) %>% 
  ungroup() %>% 
  arrange(desc(N_Dogs), desc(N_Visits)) %>% 
  rowid_to_column(var = "SequenceID") %>% 
  relocate(SequenceID, N_Dogs, N_Visits) %>% 
  filter(V1 == 2) %>% 
  kable() %>%
  kable_styling() %>% 
  add_header_above(header = c(" " = 3, "Drug Sequence (Drug Used by Visit Number)" = 10))
```

Table 41 shows the contingency table (2-way crosstabulation) of the drug used at visit 1 versus the drug used at visit 2. The cell counts are the number of patients who had a pattern that started with the indicated pair drugs. The NA values are missing data resulting from either use of some other drug (besides vincristine, cyclophosphamide, or doxorubicin), or from not having any data at all for the indicated visit. Note that there were two patients that only had one visit each (see Table 39 rows for SequenceID values of 3 and 33).

Code 
```{r}
#| label: tbl-v1-v2
#| tbl-cap: !expr paste0("Contingency Table of Drug Used at Visit 1 by Drug ", 
#|                       "Used at Visit 2 ",
#|                       "(N = ", length(unique(Final_Visits$Patient)), 
#|                       " Patients)")
#| warning: false

Final_Visits %>% 
  select(Patient, Visit_Number, Name) %>% 
  rename(VN = Visit_Number) %>% 
  pivot_wider(id_cols = "Patient", names_from = "VN", names_prefix = "Drug_at_Visit_", 
              values_from = "Name") %>% 
  xtabs(~Drug_at_Visit_1 + Drug_at_Visit_2, addNA = TRUE, data = .) %>% 
  addmargins() %>% 
  kable(col.names = c("Drug at Visit 1", "Vincristine", "Cyclophosphamide",
                      "Doxorubicin", "<NA>", "Sum")) %>%
  kable_styling() %>% 
  add_header_above(header = c(" " = 1, "Drug at Visit 2" = 4, " "))
```

To summarize how often each drug was used at each visit, see Table 42 for raw counts, and Figure 23 for a visualization of the percentages. These outputs strongly suggest that fitting a model that could disentangle temporal effects from drug effects would be very difficult in this sample because the conditional distribution of which drug was administered varies considerably by visit due to structured CHOP protocol: visits 1, 3, 5, 7, and 9 mostly used vincristine, visits 2 and 6 mostly used cyclophosphamide, and visits 4 and 8 mostly used doxorubicin. That confounds drug with visit.

Code 
```{r}
#| label: tbl-visit-drug
#| tbl-cap: Number of Records by Visit and Drug 

xtabs(~Visit_Number + Drug, data = Final_Visits) %>% 
  addmargins() %>% 
  kable(col.names = c("Visit", "1 Vincristine", "2 Cyclophosphamide", 
                      "3 Doxorubicin", "Sum")) %>% 
  kable_styling() %>% 
  add_header_above(., header = c(" ", "Drug" = 3, " "))
```
Code 
```{r}
#| label: fig-visit-drug
#| fig-cap: Distribution of Drug, by Visit

Final_Visits %>% 
  group_by(Visit_Number, Name, .drop = FALSE) %>% 
  summarize(N = n()) %>% 
  mutate(Percent = 100 * (N/sum(N))) %>% 
  ungroup() %>% 
  ggplot(., aes(fill = Name, y = Percent, x = Visit_Number)) + 
  geom_bar(position = "fill", stat = "identity") + 
  labs(y = "Percentage")
```
`summarise()` has grouped output by 'Visit_Number'. You can override using the
`.groups` argument.

3.9 Sickness

This section includes summaries prepared as we were responding to a peer review comment about the possibility about dogs being sick was a possible confounder.

Note

Per Dr. Masyr, “illness, medication, and hospitalization details are most relevant for patients with bands. Clinically, we know that most patients feel well and do not require medical support at the time points we are monitoring.” Therefore, we added the Sick_Type and Is_Sick variables to the data to address the comment. These variables were only filled out for the observations where Total_Bands > 0 (equivalent to Bands_Present = 1 (i.e., Yes)). That is why there are lots of missing values for those variables.

Table 16 and Table 15 respectively showed frequency distributions for the categorical Sick_Type and binary Bandemia and Is_Sick variables over the entire dataset. Below, we focus on the data in the subset of observations where Total_Bands > 0 (equivalent to Bands_Present = 1 (i.e., Yes)).

Code 
```{r}
#| label: create-Final-Visits-With-Bands

Final_Visits_With_Bands <- Final_Visits %>% 
  filter(Total_Bands > 0)
```

Table 43 shows the 2 x 2 contingency table for Is_Sick and Bandemia among observations with bands present. We can derive several insights from this, starting with the overall rates of bandemia and sickness in this subset of the data. The Sum row at the bottom of that table shows that 67.3% of observations with any bands present had bandemia. Meanwhile the Sum column on the right side of the table shows the dog was sick in only 27.1% of observations with bands present. A chi-square test based on Table 43 faild to detect an association between being sick and having bandemia among observations where bands are present.

Code 
```{r}
#| label: tbl-Is-Sick-Bandemia
#| tbl-cap: !expr paste0("Contingency Table for Is_Sick by Bandemia Among ", 
#|                       "Observations With Total_Bands > 0 ",
#|                       "(N = ", nrow(Final_Visits_With_Bands), " Visits)")
#| results: asis
#| message: false

CT <- Final_Visits_With_Bands %>% 
  xtabs(~Is_Sick + Bandemia, addNA = TRUE, data = .)
CT.CV <- cramers_v(x = CT, adjust = TRUE, ci = 0.95, alternative = "greater")

FN <- paste0("Chi-square test for independence, X^2(",
             chisq.test(x = CT)$parameter, ") = ",
             round(chisq.test(x = CT)$statistic, digits = 2),
             ", p = ", display_num(chisq.test(x = CT)$p.value), "; ",
             "Cramer's V (adjusted) = ",
             format(round(CT.CV$Cramers_v_adjusted, digits = 2), nsmall = 2),
             ", 1-tailed 95% CI = [",
             round(CT.CV$CI_low, digits = 2), ", ",
             format(CT.CV$CI_high, nsmall = 2), "].")

Final_Visits_With_Bands %>% 
  mutate(Bandemia = factor(Bandemia, levels = 0:1, labels = c("No", "Yes")),
         Is_Sick = factor(Is_Sick, levels = 0:1, labels = c("No", "Yes"))) %>% 
  xtabs(~Is_Sick + Bandemia, addNA = TRUE, data = .) %>% 
  addmargins() %>% 
  kable(digits = 1, col.names = c("Is Sick", "No", "Yes", "Sum")) %>% 
  kable_styling() %>% 
  add_header_above(header = c(" ", "Bandemia" = 2, " ")) %>% 
  footnote(kable_input = ., general = FN, , footnote_as_chunk = TRUE) %>% 
  cat()
```
Caution

Based on data in Table 43, bandemia was detected in 62.8% of the observations where the dog was not sick and 79.3% of the observations where the dog was sick. This descriptively hints at a possible association between sickness and bandemia but the difference in these two bandemia rates was not large enough to be confident there is really an association according to the chi-square test result. Note that the confidence interval for Cramer’s V in Table 43 is so wide that it spans all possible values for that measure of association.

Table 44 shows a finer breakdown of the degree of sickness present in observations with bands present. We can see that a few observations came from sick dogs that improved without any medical intervention. Over half of the observations where some amount of sickness was present were treated with medication that did not include antibiotics. Only a small number of these observations were from dogs that were hospitalized due to sickness.

Code 
```{r}
#| label: tbl-Sick-Type
#| tbl-cap: !expr paste0("Frequency Distribution for Sick_Type Among Observations ", 
#|                       "With Total_Bands > 0 ",
#|                       "(N = ", nrow(Final_Visits_With_Bands), " Visits)")
#| results: asis
#| message: false

FN <- paste("Self-limited means the dog was sick but improved without",
            "intervention.",
            "Medicated means the dog received supportive medications for",
            "gastro-intestinal distress that did not include antibiotics.") 

Final_Visits_With_Bands %>% 
  count(Sick_Type) %>% 
  mutate(Percent = 100*n/sum(n)) %>% 
  kable(digits = 1) %>% 
  kable_styling() %>% 
  footnote(kable_input = ., general = FN, , footnote_as_chunk = TRUE) %>% 
  cat()
```

5 Software Information

This section documents information that is important for reproducibility. Most users will not need to read it. It is primarily here for use by the statistician on the team.

We used R as our main computing environment and Quarto scripts to enhance reproducibility. We used RStudio as the editor to interface with R and Quarto.

  • Software chain: qmd file > RStudio > Quarto > R > knitr > md file > Pandoc > HTML file.
  • Source file: Descriptive_Analysis.qmd
  • Output file: Descriptive_Analysis_2026-01-26.html
  • Quarto 1.8.27 runs *.qmd files through R and knitr to produce *.md markdown files.
  • Pandoc 3.6.3 converts markdown files (*.md) to other formats, including LaTeX (*.tex) and HTML (*.html) among others.

# Purpose
This file is part of a research compendium [@Pierce-RN8714]. It provides some
descriptive analyses of data provided by Alison Masyr and Caitlin Eliason that
contains observations of dogs receiving CHOP chemotherapy at MSU Veterinary
Medicine Clinic (VMC) between 2016 and 2022. Some results here are used in a 
manuscript [@Eliason-RN8603].

# Setup
This section of the report documents some setup tasks that are useful to the
statistician on the team. Most readers of this report will probably want skip
directly to @sec-Results.

## Define Global Options
Global R chunk options are defined in the YAML header but local chunk options
will over-ride global options. We can temporarily disable an individual chunk by
inserting `#| eval: false` on a line at the top of the chunk.

# Results {#sec-Results}

## Patient-Level Summaries
@tbl-patient-cvv-missing and @tbl-patient-var-missing show summaries of missing 
data in the patient-level dataset. 

```{r}
#| label: tbl-patient-cvv-missing
#| tbl-cap: "Missingness Overview for Patient-Level Dataset (`Final_Patients`): 
#|          Cases, Variables, and Values"

Final_Patients %>% 
  cvv_missingness() %>% 
  kable(format = "html", digits = 1,
          col.names = c("Subset", rep(c("n", "%"), times = 3))) %>%
    kable_styling() %>%
    add_header_above(header = c(" " = 1, "Cases" = 2, "Variables" = 2, "Values" = 2))
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-patient-var-missing
#| tbl-cap: Misssingness Assessment for Variables in Patient-Level Dataset 
#|          (`Final_Patients`)

Final_Patients %>% 
var_missingness(.) %>% 
  kable(format = "html", digits = 1) %>%
  kable_styling() %>%
  add_header_above(header = c(" " = 3, "Observed Values" = 2, 
                              "Missing Values" = 2))
```

@tbl-patient-describe shows patient-level descriptive statistics for weight 
surface area, and number of visits, while @tbl-patient-Leukemic gives the 
univariate frequency distribution for leukemic status, which was a 
time-invariant patient-level characteristic within the CHOP cycle.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-patient-describe
#| tbl-cap: !expr paste0("Descriptive Statistics for Patient-Level Variables ", 
#|                       "(N = ", nrow(Final_Patients), " Patients)")
#| message: false

VNames <- c("Age_Yrs", "Weight_kg", "Surface_Area_m2", "N_Visits")

CNames <- c("Variable", "N", "Mean", "SD", "Min", "Q25", "Q50", "Q75", "Max")

Final_Patients %>% 
  select(Age_Yrs, Weight_kg, Surface_Area_m2, N_Visits) %>% 
  pivot_longer(cols = c(Age_Yrs, Weight_kg, Surface_Area_m2, N_Visits), 
               names_to = "Variable", values_to = "Value") %>% 
  mutate(Variable = factor(Variable, levels = VNames)) %>% 
  # Aggregate to one row per variable.
  group_by(Variable) %>% 
  summarise(N = sum(!is.na(Value)), 
            Mean = mean(Value, na.rm = TRUE),
            SD = sd(Value, na.rm = TRUE),
            Min = min(Value, na.rm = TRUE),
            Q25 = quantile(Value, probs = .25, na.rm = TRUE),
            Q50 = quantile(Value, probs = .50, na.rm = TRUE),
            Q75 = quantile(Value, probs = .75, na.rm = TRUE),
            Max = max(Value, na.rm = TRUE)) %>% 
  kable(., format = "html", digits = 2, 
        col.names = CNames, row.names = FALSE) %>% 
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"),
                fixed_thead = T)
```

```{r}
#| label: weight

N_Weight_LT10 <- Final_Patients %>% filter(Weight_kg < 10) %>% nrow()
N_Weight_1015 <- Final_Patients %>% filter(between(Weight_kg, left = 10, right = 15)) %>% nrow()

Pct_Weight_LT10 <- 100*N_Weight_LT10/nrow(Final_Patients)
Pct_Weight_1015 <- 100*N_Weight_1015/nrow(Final_Patients)
```

:::{.callout-tip}
Below are specific statistics about numbers and percentage of patients at the 
very low end of weight distribution that we use in the manuscript.

* `r N_Weight_LT10` (`r round(Pct_Weight_LT10, digits = 0)`%) weighed less than 
  10 kg.
* `r N_Weight_1015` (`r round(Pct_Weight_1015, digits = 0)`%) weighed 10-15 kg.

:::

```{r}
#| label: tbl-patient-Sex
#| tbl-cap: !expr paste0("Frequency Distribution for Sex ", 
#|                       "(N = ", nrow(Final_Patients), " Patients)")
#| message: false

Final_Patients %>% 
  xtabs(~Sex, addNA = TRUE, data = .) %>% 
  as.data.frame() %>% 
  mutate(Percent = 100*Freq/nrow(Final_Patients)) %>% 
  kable(., format = "html", digits = 0) %>% 
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"),
                fixed_thead = T)
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-patient-Sex-Neutered
#| tbl-cap: !expr paste0("Contingency Table for Sex by Neutered Status", 
#|                       " Status (N = ", nrow(Final_Patients), " Patients)")
#| message: false

Final_Patients %>% 
  xtabs(~Sex + Neutered, addNA = TRUE, data = .) %>% 
  as.data.frame() %>% 
  pivot_wider(names_from = Neutered, values_from = Freq) %>% 
  kable(., format = "html", digits = 0) %>% 
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"),
                fixed_thead = T)
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-patient-Breed
#| tbl-cap: !expr paste0("Frequency Distribution for Breed ", 
#|                       "(N = ", nrow(Final_Patients), " Patients)")
#| message: false

Final_Patients %>% 
  xtabs(~Breed, addNA = TRUE, data = .) %>% 
  as.data.frame() %>% 
  arrange(desc(Freq), Breed) %>% 
  mutate(Percent = 100*Freq/nrow(Final_Patients)) %>% 
  kable(., format = "html", digits = 0) %>% 
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"),
                fixed_thead = T)
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-patient-Diagnosis
#| tbl-cap: !expr paste0("Frequency Distribution for Diagnosis ", 
#|                       "(N = ", nrow(Final_Patients), " Patients)")
#| message: false

Final_Patients %>% 
  xtabs(~Diagnosis, addNA = TRUE, data = .) %>% 
  as.data.frame() %>% 
  arrange(desc(Freq), Diagnosis) %>% 
  mutate(Percent = 100*Freq/nrow(Final_Patients)) %>% 
  kable(., format = "html", digits = 0) %>% 
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"),
                fixed_thead = T)
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-patient-Stage
#| tbl-cap: !expr paste0("Frequency Distribution for Lymphoma Stage ", 
#|                       "(N = ", nrow(Final_Patients), " Patients)")
#| message: false

Final_Patients %>% 
  xtabs(~Stage, addNA = TRUE, data = .) %>% 
  as.data.frame() %>% 
  mutate(Percent = 100*Freq/nrow(Final_Patients)) %>% 
  kable(., format = "html", digits = 0) %>% 
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"),
                fixed_thead = T)
```

:::{.callout-caution}
Using `Stage` as a predictor in the model would be complicated by the fact that 
there is only one patient with `Stage = 1` and none with `Stage = 2`. Meanwhile, 
some patients have missing `Stage` data because they have diseases to which
staging does not apply, while others just have true missing data. Given the size 
and heterogeneity of the sample, I think omitting `Stage` as a model predictor 
of bandemia seems like the wiser choice.
:::

```{r}
#| label: tbl-patient-Substage
#| tbl-cap: !expr paste0("Frequency Distribution for Lymphoma Substage ", 
#|                       "(N = ", nrow(Final_Patients), " Patients)")
#| message: false

Final_Patients %>% 
  xtabs(~Substage, addNA = TRUE, data = .) %>% 
  as.data.frame() %>% 
  mutate(Percent = 100*Freq/nrow(Final_Patients)) %>% 
  kable(., format = "html", digits = 0) %>% 
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"),
                fixed_thead = T)
```

:::{.callout-caution}
The concerns about using `Stage` as a predictor in the model also extend to
`Substage` Given the size and heterogeneity of the sample, omitting `Substage`
as a model predictor of bandemia seems like the wiser choice.
:::

```{r}
#| label: tbl-patient-Phenotype
#| tbl-cap: !expr paste0("Frequency Distribution for Lymphoma Phenotype ", 
#|                       "(N = ", nrow(Final_Patients), " Patients)")
#| message: false

Final_Patients %>% 
  xtabs(~Phenotype, addNA = TRUE, data = .) %>% 
  as.data.frame() %>% 
  mutate(Percent = 100*Freq/nrow(Final_Patients)) %>% 
  kable(., format = "html", digits = 0) %>% 
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"),
                fixed_thead = T)
```

:::{.callout-caution}
The amount of missing data for `Phenotype` poses a problem for using it as a
predictor in the model. Some of that may be a result of that property not being
relevant to some of the diagnoses in the sample. Omitting `Phenotype` as a model
predictor of bandemia seems like the wiser choice.
:::



## Visit-Level Summaries
@tbl-visit-cvv-missing and @tbl-visit-var-missing show summaries of missing 
data in the visit-level dataset. 

```{r}
#| label: tbl-visit-cvv-missing
#| tbl-cap: "Missingness Overview for Visit-Level Dataset (`Final_visits`): 
#|          Cases, Variables, and Values"

Final_Visits %>% 
  cvv_missingness() %>% 
  kable(format = "html", digits = 1,
          col.names = c("Subset", rep(c("n", "%"), times = 3))) %>%
    kable_styling() %>%
    add_header_above(header = c(" " = 1, "Cases" = 2, "Variables" = 2, "Values" = 2))
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-visit-var-missing
#| tbl-cap: Misssingness Assessment for Variables in Visit-Level Dataset 
#|          (`Final_Visits`)

Final_Visits %>% 
var_missingness(.) %>% 
  #arrange(desc(Pct_Missing)) %>%   # Sort by % missing
  kable(format = "html", digits = 1) %>%
  kable_styling() %>%
  add_header_above(header = c(" " = 3, "Observed Values" = 2, 
                              "Missing Values" = 2))
```

@tbl-visit-describe-cat shows univariate frequency distributions for binary 
categorical biomarker variables. The `Is_Sick` variable is a binary transform 
of `Sick_Type`; it has a lot of missing values because we only collected 
`Sick_Type` for observations with `Total_Bands > 0` (equivalent to 
`Bands_Present = 1 (i.e., Yes)`). 

```{r}
#| label: tbl-visit-describe-cat
#| tbl-cap: !expr paste0("Descriptive Statistics for Categorical Biomarker ", 
#|                       "Variables (N = ", nrow(Final_Visits), " Visits)")
#| message: false

VNames <- c("Bands_Present", "Bandemia", "High_BN_Ratio", "Is_Sick", 
            "Toxic_Change")

Final_Visits %>% 
  select(Bands_Present, Bandemia, High_BN_Ratio, Is_Sick, Toxic_Change) %>% 
  pivot_longer(cols = c(Bands_Present, Bandemia, High_BN_Ratio, Is_Sick, 
                        Toxic_Change), 
               names_to = "Variable", values_to = "Value") %>% 
  group_by(Variable, Value, .drop = FALSE) %>% 
  summarise(N = n()) %>% 
  mutate(Variable = factor(Variable, levels = VNames),
         Value = factor(Value, levels=0:1, labels = c("No", "Yes")),
         Percent = 100*(N/nrow(Final_Visits))) %>% 
  arrange(Variable, desc(Value)) %>% 
  mutate(Variable = factor(Variable, levels = VNames)) %>% 
  kable(., format = "html", digits = 1, row.names = FALSE) %>% 
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"),
                fixed_thead = T) %>% 
  collapse_rows(., columns = 1, valign = "top", 
                row_group_label_position = "stack") 
```

@tbl-visit-Sick-Type shows the frequency distribution of the 4-level `Sick_Type` 
variable across all observations. This variable has a lot of missing values 
because we only collected `Sick_Type` for observations with `Total_Bands > 0` 
(equivalent to `Bands_Present = 1 (i.e., Yes)`). Self-limited means that 
sickness was not treated with either medication or hospitalization. 

```{r}
#| label: tbl-visit-Sick-Type
#| tbl-cap: !expr paste0("Frequency Distribution for Sick Type ", 
#|                       "(N = ", nrow(Final_Visits), " Visits)")
#| message: false

Final_Visits %>% 
  count(Sick_Type) %>% 
  rename(N_Visits = n) %>% 
  mutate(Percent = 100*(N_Visits/nrow(Final_Visits))) %>% 
  kbl(digits = 1) %>%
  kable_styling()
```


@tbl-visit-band-category shows the frequency distribution for 3-level ordinal 
band category variable. 

```{r}
#| label: tbl-visit-band-category
#| tbl-cap: !expr paste0("Frequency Distribution for Band Category ", 
#|                       "(N = ", nrow(Final_Visits), " Visits)")
#| message: false

Final_Visits %>% 
  count(Band_Category) %>% 
  rename(N_Visits = n) %>% 
  mutate(Percent = 100*(N_Visits/nrow(Final_Visits))) %>% 
  kbl(digits = 1) %>%
  kable_styling()
```

@tbl-visit-bands-toxic shows the crosstabulation of whether bands were present 
and whether toxic change was observed in the CBC sample in the visit-level data. 
This was initially used to investigate missing data issues that we have 
subsequently fixed. 

```{r}
#| label: tbl-visit-bands-toxic
#| tbl-cap: !expr paste0("Crosstab of Bands Present by Toxic Change ", 
#|                       "(N = ", nrow(Final_Visits), " Visits)")

Final_Visits %>% 
  mutate(Bands_Present = factor(Bands_Present, levels = 0:1, 
                                labels = c("No", "Yes")),
         Toxic_Change = factor(Toxic_Change, levels = 0:1, 
                                labels = c("No", "Yes"))) %>% 
  xtabs(~Toxic_Change + Bands_Present , addNA = TRUE, data = .) %>% 
  addmargins() %>% 
  as.data.frame() %>% 
  pivot_wider(names_from = Bands_Present, values_from = Freq) %>% 
  kable(., format = "html", digits = 1, row.names = FALSE) %>% 
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"),
                fixed_thead = T) %>% 
  row_spec(row = 3, italic = TRUE) %>% 
  column_spec(column = 4, italic = TRUE) %>% 
  add_header_above(header = c(" ", "Bands_Present" = 2, " "))
```

:::{.callout-tip}
@tbl-visit-bands-toxic shows that all of the instances of toxic change are for 
CBC samples where bands were present. Per Dr. Masyr, toxic change is a 
description given to mature neutrophils, not bands (though both can be 
simultaneously present). 
:::

@tbl-visit-describe-cont shows visit-level descriptive statistics for continuous 
biomarker variables, while @tbl-visit-describe-cont-by-Bandemia repeats the same 
summary broken down by whether banedmia was absent versus present at the time of 
the CBC sample. 

```{r}
#| label: tbl-visit-describe-cont
#| tbl-cap: !expr paste0("Descriptive Statistics for Continuous Biomarker ", 
#|                       "Variables (N = ", nrow(Final_Visits), " Visits)")
#| message: false

VNames <- c("Total_WBC", "Total_Neutrophil", "Total_Bands", "BN_Ratio")
VNamesUnits <- c("Total_WBC (k/ul)", 
                 "Total_Neutrophil (k/ul)", 
                 "Total_Bands (k/ul)", 
                 "BN_Ratio")

CNames <- c("Variable", "N", "Mean", "SD", "Min", "Q25", "Q50", "Q75", "Max")

Final_Visits %>% 
  select(Total_WBC, Total_Neutrophil, Total_Bands, BN_Ratio) %>% 
  pivot_longer(cols = c(Total_WBC, Total_Neutrophil, Total_Bands, BN_Ratio), 
               names_to = "Variable", values_to = "Value") %>% 
  mutate(Variable = factor(Variable, levels = VNames)) %>% 
  # Aggregate to one row per variable.
  group_by(Variable) %>% 
  summarise(N = sum(!is.na(Value)), 
            Mean = mean(Value, na.rm = TRUE),
            SD = sd(Value, na.rm = TRUE),
            Min = min(Value, na.rm = TRUE),
            Q25 = quantile(Value, probs = .25, na.rm = TRUE),
            Q50 = quantile(Value, probs = .50, na.rm = TRUE),
            Q75 = quantile(Value, probs = .75, na.rm = TRUE),
            Max = max(Value, na.rm = TRUE)) %>% 
  ungroup() %>% 
  mutate(Variable = factor(Variable, levels = VNames, labels = VNamesUnits)) %>% 
  kable(., format = "html", digits = 1, 
        col.names = CNames, row.names = FALSE) %>% 
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"),
                fixed_thead = T) 
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-visit-bands-neuts
#| fig-cap: !expr paste0("Scatterplot of Total Bands and Total Neutrophils ", 
#|                       "With Linear and Loess Smoothing Curves ",
#|                       "(N = ", nrow(Final_Visits), " Visits)")
#| fig-width: 4
#| fig-height: 2.64
#| warning: false

Fig1 <- Final_Visits %>% 
  ggplot(., aes(x = Total_Neutrophil, y = Total_Bands)) + 
  geom_point() +
  stat_correlation(method = "pearson", small.r = TRUE, r.conf.level = 0.95, 
                   use_label("R", "R.CI", "n")) +
  geom_smooth(method="loess", se = TRUE, fullrange = FALSE, 
              level = 0.95, linetype = "dashed", col = "red") +
  geom_smooth(method="lm", se = TRUE, fullrange = FALSE, level = 0.95, 
              linetype = "solid", col = "red") +
  theme_bw() +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, 50), ylim = c(0, 7), ) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(from = 0, to = 50, by = 10)) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(from = 0, to = 7, by = 1)) +
  xlab("Total neutrophils (k/ul)") +
  ylab("Total bands (k/ul)") +
  annotate(geom = "text", x =45, y = 4.6, label = "Loess", col = "red") +
  annotate(geom = "text", x =45, y = 2.5, label = "Linear", col = "red") 

Fig1

# Export figure for use in journal submission
ggsave(filename = here(paste0("scripts/output/Figure_1.png")), plot = Fig1, 
       device = "png", width = 4, height = 2.64, units = "in", dpi = 600)
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-visit-describe-Dose-by-Drug
#| tbl-cap: !expr paste0("Descriptive Statistics for Dosage ", 
#|                       "by Drug (N = ", nrow(Final_Visits), 
#|                       " Visits)")
#| message: false

VNames <- c("Dose_mgpm2")
VNamesUnits <- c("Dosage (mg/m^2)")

CNames <- c("Drug", "Variable", "N", "Mean", "SD", "Min", "Q25", "Q50", 
            "Q75", "Max")

Final_Visits %>% 
  select(Name, Dose_mgpm2) %>% 
  pivot_longer(cols = c(Dose_mgpm2), 
               names_to = "Variable", values_to = "Value") %>% 
  mutate(Variable = factor(VNames, levels = VNames)) %>% 
  # Aggregate to one row per variable.
  group_by(Name) %>% 
  summarise(Variable = VNames,
            N = sum(!is.na(Value)), 
            Mean = mean(Value, na.rm = TRUE),
            SD = sd(Value, na.rm = TRUE),
            Min = min(Value, na.rm = TRUE),
            Q25 = quantile(Value, probs = .25, na.rm = TRUE),
            Q50 = quantile(Value, probs = .50, na.rm = TRUE),
            Q75 = quantile(Value, probs = .75, na.rm = TRUE),
            Max = max(Value, na.rm = TRUE)) %>% 
  ungroup() %>% 
  mutate(Variable = factor(Variable, levels = VNames, labels = VNamesUnits)) %>% 
  kable(., format = "html", digits = 1, 
        col.names = CNames, row.names = FALSE) %>% 
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"),
                fixed_thead = T) 
```

:::{.callout-caution}
Dosage is a visit-level (L1) variable. The three drugs have very different
ranges of typical values for dosage: The ranges differ by multiple orders of
magnitude. Furthermore, there is no good reason expect that the dosage effect
would have the same slope for across drugs. To use dosage in the model, we would
need to center it, aggregate it to L2 means, then include main effect and 
interaction terms at both L1 and L2 between dosage and drug. We would also need 
to consider non-linear dosage effects. The interactions would permit the 
dosage effect to vary across drugs but this, plus considering non-linearity, 
would add a lot of parameters to the model. Given the sample size, that seems
overly ambitious. It seems better to omit dosage effects from the model. I am 
not confident our data are sufficient to get reliable findings about dosage 
effects. 
:::

## Total Bands
@tbl-freq-bands shows the frequency distribution for total bands in both its 
original units (x10.e3/uL=k/uL) and log-transformed units. It highlights the 
large proportion of zero values. 

```{r}
#| label: tbl-freq-bands
#| tbl-cap: "Frequency Distribution of Total Bands for All Visits"

Final_Visits %>% 
  count(Total_Bands) %>% 
  mutate(Log_Total_Bands = log(Total_Bands), 
         Proportion = n/nrow(Final_Visits)) %>% 
  select(Total_Bands, Log_Total_Bands, n, Proportion) %>% 
  kable(digits = 3, col.names = c("Total Bands (k/ul)", 
                                  "log(Total Bands [k/ul])", 
                                  "n", 
                                  "Proportion")) %>%
  kable_styling() %>% 
  add_header_above(header = c("Raw Values", "Transformed Values" = 1, 
                              "Frequency" = 2))
```

@fig-bands shows the distribution total bands in the original units via a
histogram. The heavy concentration of zero values makes it hard to see the shape 
of the distribution among the non-zero values.

```{r}
#| label: fig-bands
#| fig-cap: Distribution of Total Bands (k/ul) for All Visits.
#| fig-width: 6
#| fig-height: 3
#| message: false

ggplot(Final_Visits, aes(x = Total_Bands)) + 
  geom_histogram(aes(y=after_stat(count)), colour="black", fill="grey70") +
  theme_bw() +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(-0.2,7), n.breaks = 8, oob = function(x, limits) x) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits=c(-0.2, 500)) +
  xlab("Total Bands (k/ul)") +
  ylab("No. of Patients")
```

@fig-log-bands shows the distribution of log-transformed total bands via both a
histogram and a boxplot with jittered data points. It includes data from all 
visits. In both graphs, the log equals -Infinity when total bands are 0, so we
recoded these values to improve the figures and keep them compact and readable.

```{r}
#| label: fig-log-bands
#| fig-cap: Distribution of log(Total Bands [k/ul]) for All Visits.
#| fig-width: 6
#| fig-height: 4
#| message: false

p1 <- Final_Visits %>% 
  ggplot(., aes(x = log_Total_Bands)) + 
  geom_histogram(aes(y=after_stat(count)), colour="black", fill="grey70") +
  theme_bw() +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(-5.1, 2), breaks = c(-5, -3:2), 
                     labels = c("-Inf", as.character(-3:2)),
                     oob = function(x, limits) x) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits=c(-0.1, 500)) +
  xlab("log(Total Bands [k/ul])") +
  ylab("No. of Patients") +
  ggtitle("Histogram")

p2 <- Final_Visits %>% 
  ggplot(., aes(x = log_Total_Bands, y = "")) +
  geom_jitter(alpha = .3, height = .25, width = .05) +
  geom_boxplot(outliers = FALSE, alpha = .5) +
  theme_bw() +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(-5, 2)) +
  scale_y_discrete( ) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(-5.1, 2), breaks = c(-5, -3:2), 
                     labels = c("-Inf", as.character(-3:2))) +
  xlab("log(Total Bands [k/ul])")  + 
  ylab(" ")  +
  ggtitle("Boxplot")

p1 + p2 + 
  plot_layout(nrow = 2, heights = c(3,1)) + 
  plot_annotation(tag_levels = "A")
```

@tbl-drug-Band-Category and @fig-drug-Band-Category show the number and percent

```{r}
#| label: tbl-drug-Band-Category
#| tbl-cap: Band Category Frequency by Prior Drug Administered

Drug1_N <- Final_Visits %>% filter(Drug == 1) %>% nrow()
Drug2_N <- Final_Visits %>% filter(Drug == 2) %>% nrow()
Drug3_N <- Final_Visits %>% filter(Drug == 3) %>% nrow()

Drug_Band_Category <- Final_Visits %>% 
  xtabs(~Band_Category + Drug, data = .) %>% 
  addmargins(margin = 1) %>% 
  as.data.frame() %>% 
  rename(N = Freq) %>% 
  mutate(Name = factor(Drug, labels = DrugNames), 
         Percent = case_when(Drug == 1 ~ 100*N/Drug1_N,
                             Drug == 2 ~ 100*N/Drug2_N,
                             Drug == 3 ~ 100*N/Drug3_N)) %>% 
  relocate(Drug, Name, Band_Category) 

Drug_Band_Category %>% 
  kable(digits = 1, 
        col.names = c("Drug", "Name", "Band Category", "N", "Percent")) %>% 
  kable_styling()
```

```{r}
  # coord_cartesian(ylim = c(-5, 2)) +
  # scale_y_continuous(limits = c(-5.1, 2), breaks = c(-5, -3:2), 
  #                    labels = c("-Inf", as.character(-3:2))) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(-3, 2)) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(-3, 2), breaks = c(-3:2)) +
  xlab("Visit Number") +
  ylab("log(Total Bands [k/ul])")

p1 + p2 +
 plot_layout(nrow = 2) + 
 plot_annotation(tag_levels = "A")
```

in the manuscript. We used a variation of panel A as Figure 3 in the prior 
manuscript, which we are now revising for submission to another journal.

## Bandemia by Visit Number
@tbl-bandemia-by-visit and @fig-bandemia-by-visit show that there is not a
simple functional form for the relationship between visit number and bandemia
rate. It is probably not viable to model a visit effect in this study because of
this and because of the structural association of visit number with which drug
was used (see @fig-visit-drug in the Drug Sequences section). Also note that the
bandemia rate at visit 10 should be interpreted with caution because of the tiny
sample size.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-bandemia-by-visit
#| tbl-cap: Bandemia Rate by Visit Number

Final_Visits %>% 
  group_by(Visit_Number) %>% 
  summarize(N = n(),
            Bandemia = mean(Bandemia)) %>%
  kable(format = "html", digits = 2) %>% 
  kable_styling()
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-bandemia-by-visit
#| fig-cap: Bandemia Rate by Visit Number

Final_Visits %>% 
  group_by(Visit_Number) %>% 
  summarize(Bandemia = mean(Bandemia)) %>%
  ggplot(., aes(x = Visit_Number, y = Bandemia)) + 
  geom_bar(stat = "identity") + 
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(1:10), minor_breaks = NULL) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0,.36), 
                     breaks = seq(from = 0, to = .35, by = .05),
                     minor_breaks = NULL) +
  theme_bw()
```

## Drug Sequences
@tbl-visit-patterns shows the frequency of occurrence for each unique sequence 
of drug use observed. Each row represents a group of dogs who got the same
sequence of drugs across the 10 visits of interest. Ideally, the most common
sequence will match the intended CHOP protocol sequence for using the drugs. The
table is sorted in descending order by sequence frequency (`N_Dogs`) then by
`N_Visits`, which is the number of visits in the pattern that were actually
observed. Columns `V1` to `V10` show the drug number used at a specific visit
number in the given sequence. Because only data about drugs 1-3 were included,
it is possible that blanks in the middle of a sequence were visits where some
other drug was administered.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-visit-patterns
#| tbl-cap: !expr paste0("Frequency Distribution of Drug Sequence ", 
#|                       "(N = ", length(unique(Final_Visits$Patient)), 
#|                       " Patients)")
#| warning: false

options(knitr.kable.NA = '-')

Final_Visits %>% 
  select(Patient, Visit_Number, Drug) %>% 
  rename(VN = Visit_Number) %>% 
  pivot_wider(id_cols = "Patient", names_from = "VN", names_prefix = "V", 
              values_from = "Drug") %>% 
  group_by(V1, V2, V3, V4, V5, V6, V7, V8, V9, V10) %>% 
  summarize(N_Dogs = n()) %>% 
  ungroup() %>% 
  rowwise() %>% 
  mutate(N_Visits = sum(!is.na(c_across(V1:V10)))) %>% 
  ungroup() %>% 
  arrange(desc(N_Dogs), desc(N_Visits)) %>% 
  rowid_to_column(var = "SequenceID") %>% 
  relocate(SequenceID, N_Dogs, N_Visits) %>% 
  kable() %>%
  kable_styling() %>% 
  add_header_above(header = c(" " = 3, "Drug Sequence (Drug Used by Visit Number)" = 10))
```

@tbl-visit-patterns-subset shows the subset of drug sequences that deviate from 
the CHOP protocol by using cyclosphosphamide at visit 1. 

```{r}
#| label: tbl-visit-patterns-subset
#| tbl-cap: !expr paste0("Subset of Drug Sequences That Used Cyclosphosphamide ", 
#|                       "at Visit 1 ",
#|                       "(N = ", length(unique(Final_Visits$Patient)), 
#|                       " Patients)")
#| warning: false

options(knitr.kable.NA = '-')

Final_Visits %>% 
  select(Patient, Visit_Number, Drug) %>% 
  rename(VN = Visit_Number) %>% 
  pivot_wider(id_cols = "Patient", names_from = "VN", names_prefix = "V", 
              values_from = "Drug") %>% 
  group_by(V1, V2, V3, V4, V5, V6, V7, V8, V9, V10) %>% 
  summarize(N_Dogs = n()) %>% 
  ungroup() %>% 
  rowwise() %>% 
  mutate(N_Visits = sum(!is.na(c_across(V1:V10)))) %>% 
  ungroup() %>% 
  arrange(desc(N_Dogs), desc(N_Visits)) %>% 
  rowid_to_column(var = "SequenceID") %>% 
  relocate(SequenceID, N_Dogs, N_Visits) %>% 
  filter(V1 == 2) %>% 
  kable() %>%
  kable_styling() %>% 
  add_header_above(header = c(" " = 3, "Drug Sequence (Drug Used by Visit Number)" = 10))
```

@tbl-v1-v2 shows the contingency table (2-way crosstabulation) of the drug used 
at visit 1 versus the drug used at visit 2. The cell counts are the number of 
patients who had a pattern that started with the indicated pair drugs. The NA 
values are missing data resulting from either use of some other drug (besides 
vincristine, cyclophosphamide, or doxorubicin), or from not having any data at 
all for the indicated visit. Note that there were two patients that only had one 
visit each (see @tbl-visit-patterns rows for `SequenceID` values of 3 and 33).

```{r}
#| label: tbl-v1-v2
#| tbl-cap: !expr paste0("Contingency Table of Drug Used at Visit 1 by Drug ", 
#|                       "Used at Visit 2 ",
#|                       "(N = ", length(unique(Final_Visits$Patient)), 
#|                       " Patients)")
#| warning: false

Final_Visits %>% 
  select(Patient, Visit_Number, Name) %>% 
  rename(VN = Visit_Number) %>% 
  pivot_wider(id_cols = "Patient", names_from = "VN", names_prefix = "Drug_at_Visit_", 
              values_from = "Name") %>% 
  xtabs(~Drug_at_Visit_1 + Drug_at_Visit_2, addNA = TRUE, data = .) %>% 
  addmargins() %>% 
  kable(col.names = c("Drug at Visit 1", "Vincristine", "Cyclophosphamide",
                      "Doxorubicin", "<NA>", "Sum")) %>%
  kable_styling() %>% 
  add_header_above(header = c(" " = 1, "Drug at Visit 2" = 4, " "))
```

To summarize how often each drug was used at each visit, see @tbl-visit-drug for
raw counts, and @fig-visit-drug for a visualization of the percentages. These
outputs strongly suggest that fitting a model that could disentangle temporal
effects from drug effects would be very difficult in this sample because the
conditional distribution of which drug was administered varies considerably by
visit due to structured CHOP protocol: visits 1, 3, 5, 7, and 9 mostly used
vincristine, visits 2 and 6 mostly used cyclophosphamide, and visits 4 and 8
mostly used doxorubicin. That confounds drug with visit.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-visit-drug
#| tbl-cap: Number of Records by Visit and Drug 

xtabs(~Visit_Number + Drug, data = Final_Visits) %>% 
  addmargins() %>% 
  kable(col.names = c("Visit", "1 Vincristine", "2 Cyclophosphamide", 
                      "3 Doxorubicin", "Sum")) %>% 
  kable_styling() %>% 
  add_header_above(., header = c(" ", "Drug" = 3, " "))
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-visit-drug
#| fig-cap: Distribution of Drug, by Visit

Final_Visits %>% 
  group_by(Visit_Number, Name, .drop = FALSE) %>% 
  summarize(N = n()) %>% 
  mutate(Percent = 100 * (N/sum(N))) %>% 
  ungroup() %>% 
  ggplot(., aes(fill = Name, y = Percent, x = Visit_Number)) + 
  geom_bar(position = "fill", stat = "identity") + 
  labs(y = "Percentage")
```

## Sickness
This section includes summaries prepared as we were responding to a peer review 
comment about the possibility about dogs being sick was a possible confounder. 

:::{.callout-note}
Per Dr. Masyr, "illness, medication, and hospitalization details are 
most relevant for patients with bands. Clinically, we know that most patients 
feel well and do not require medical support at the time points we are 
monitoring." Therefore, we added the `Sick_Type` and `Is_Sick` variables to the 
data to address the comment. These variables were only filled out for the 
observations where `Total_Bands` > 0 (equivalent to 
`Bands_Present = 1 (i.e., Yes)`). That is why there are lots of missing values
for those variables. 
:::

@tbl-visit-Sick-Type and @tbl-visit-describe-cat respectively showed frequency 
distributions for the categorical `Sick_Type` and binary `Bandemia` and 
`Is_Sick` variables over the entire dataset. Below, we focus on the data in the 
subset of observations where `Total_Bands` > 0 (equivalent to 
`Bands_Present = 1 (i.e., Yes)`). 

```{r}
#| label: create-Final-Visits-With-Bands

Final_Visits_With_Bands <- Final_Visits %>% 
  filter(Total_Bands > 0)
```

@tbl-Is-Sick-Bandemia shows the 2 x 2 contingency table for `Is_Sick` and 
`Bandemia` among observations with bands present. We can derive several insights 
from this, starting with the overall rates of bandemia and sickness in this 
subset of the data. The Sum row at the bottom of that table shows that 
`r round(mean(Final_Visits_With_Bands$Bandemia)*100, digits = 1)`% of 
observations with any bands present had bandemia. Meanwhile the Sum column on 
the right side of the table shows the dog was sick in only 
`r round(mean(Final_Visits_With_Bands$Is_Sick)*100, digits = 1)`% of 
observations with bands present. A chi-square test based on
@tbl-Is-Sick-Bandemia faild to detect an association between being sick and
having bandemia among observations where bands are present. 

```{r}
#| label: tbl-Is-Sick-Bandemia
#| tbl-cap: !expr paste0("Contingency Table for Is_Sick by Bandemia Among ", 
#|                       "Observations With Total_Bands > 0 ",
#|                       "(N = ", nrow(Final_Visits_With_Bands), " Visits)")
#| results: asis
#| message: false

CT <- Final_Visits_With_Bands %>% 
  xtabs(~Is_Sick + Bandemia, addNA = TRUE, data = .)
CT.CV <- cramers_v(x = CT, adjust = TRUE, ci = 0.95, alternative = "greater")

FN <- paste0("Chi-square test for independence, X^2(",
             chisq.test(x = CT)$parameter, ") = ",
             round(chisq.test(x = CT)$statistic, digits = 2),
             ", p = ", display_num(chisq.test(x = CT)$p.value), "; ",
             "Cramer's V (adjusted) = ",
             format(round(CT.CV$Cramers_v_adjusted, digits = 2), nsmall = 2),
             ", 1-tailed 95% CI = [",
             round(CT.CV$CI_low, digits = 2), ", ",
             format(CT.CV$CI_high, nsmall = 2), "].")

Final_Visits_With_Bands %>% 
  mutate(Bandemia = factor(Bandemia, levels = 0:1, labels = c("No", "Yes")),
         Is_Sick = factor(Is_Sick, levels = 0:1, labels = c("No", "Yes"))) %>% 
  xtabs(~Is_Sick + Bandemia, addNA = TRUE, data = .) %>% 
  addmargins() %>% 
  kable(digits = 1, col.names = c("Is Sick", "No", "Yes", "Sum")) %>% 
  kable_styling() %>% 
  add_header_above(header = c(" ", "Bandemia" = 2, " ")) %>% 
  footnote(kable_input = ., general = FN, , footnote_as_chunk = TRUE) %>% 
  cat()
```

:::{.callout-caution}
Based on data in @tbl-Is-Sick-Bandemia, bandemia was detected 
in `r round(100*CT[1,2]/sum(CT[1,]), digits = 1)`% of the observations where the 
dog was not sick and `r round(100*CT[2,2]/sum(CT[2,]), digits = 1)`% of the 
observations where the dog was sick. This descriptively hints at a possible
association between sickness and bandemia but the difference in these two
bandemia rates was not large enough to be confident there is really an
association according to the chi-square test result. Note that the confidence
interval for Cramer's V in @tbl-Is-Sick-Bandemia is so wide that it spans all
possible values for that measure of association.
:::

@tbl-Sick-Type shows a finer breakdown of the degree of sickness present in 
observations with bands present. We can see that a few observations came from 
sick dogs that improved without any medical intervention. Over half of 
the observations where some amount of sickness was present were treated with 
medication that did not include antibiotics. Only a small number of these 
observations were from dogs that were hospitalized due to sickness.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-Sick-Type
#| tbl-cap: !expr paste0("Frequency Distribution for Sick_Type Among Observations ", 
#|                       "With Total_Bands > 0 ",
#|                       "(N = ", nrow(Final_Visits_With_Bands), " Visits)")
#| results: asis
#| message: false

FN <- paste("Self-limited means the dog was sick but improved without",
            "intervention.",
            "Medicated means the dog received supportive medications for",
            "gastro-intestinal distress that did not include antibiotics.") 

Final_Visits_With_Bands %>% 
  count(Sick_Type) %>% 
  mutate(Percent = 100*n/sum(n)) %>% 
  kable(digits = 1) %>% 
  kable_styling() %>% 
  footnote(kable_input = ., general = FN, , footnote_as_chunk = TRUE) %>% 
  cat()
```

# Software Information
This section documents information that is important for reproducibility. Most
users will not need to read it. It is primarily here for use by the statistician
on the team.

We used [R](https://www.r-project.org/) as our main computing environment and
[Quarto](https://quarto.org/) scripts to enhance reproducibility. We used
[RStudio](www.rstudio.org) as the editor to interface with R and Quarto.

- Software chain:
  **qmd file > RStudio > Quarto > R > knitr > md file > Pandoc > HTML file**.
- Source file: **`r params$SourceFile`**
- Output file: **`r params$LogFile`**
- [Quarto `r quarto_version()`](https://quarto.org/) runs `*.qmd` files through 
  [R](https://www.r-project.org/) and [knitr](https://yihui.org/knitr/) to 
  produce `*.md` markdown files.
- [Pandoc `r rmarkdown::pandoc_version()`](https://pandoc.org) converts markdown 
  files (`*.md`) to other formats, including LaTeX (`*.tex`) and HTML (`*.html`) 
  among others.
